headings: Risks Related to our Business and the Oil and Natural Gas Industry
If we are unable to replace oil and natural gas reserves, we may not be able to sustain or grow our business.
Future exploration and drilling results are uncertain and involve substantial costs.
Our current operations are primarily concentrated in a single geographic region, making us vulnerable to regional risks.
Global geopolitical tensions may increase volatility in oil, gas and NGL prices and could adversely affect our business.
Our actual recovery of reserves may differ substantially from our proved reserve estimates.
We risk losing leases if we cannot drill before such leases expire.
We depend on infrastructure to market and deliver our production.
Inflation and interest rate changes could increase our costs.
We may not be able to obtain sufficient surety bonds on reasonably acceptable terms to conduct our business.
Technology and cybersecurity threats could disrupt our operations and cause reputational and financial harm to our business.
We have limited control over the activities on properties we do not operate.
Hedging transactions may limit our potential gains and expose us to other risks.
Compliance with environmental laws, including legal requirements related to marine life and endangered and threatened species, could increase our costs and limit operations.
Production shut-ins could increase costs and reduce future production.
Severe weather or public health events could disrupt production and reduce revenues.
We are not insured against all of the operating risks to which our business is exposed.
Our actual production could differ materially from our forecasts.
Intense industry competition could limit our growth and increase costs.
The loss of a significant customer could materially reduce our revenue and materially adversely affect our business.
We rely on skilled and experienced personnel, and shortages in such personnel, higher labor costs or the loss of key management could adversely affect our ability to operate.
We have various contractual commitments. Our failure to satisfy these commitments could adversely affect our results of operations and financial position.
Our Mexican operations are subject to evolving regulatory and environmental requirements that could increase costs and create compliance risks.
Seismic data interpretation does not guarantee the presence of commercially viable hydrocarbons.
Violation of anti-corruption laws, including the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, could result in severe penalties and loss of key contracts.

Our business faces risks related to climate change concerns that could increase our operating costs, restrict where we can operate, and reduce demand for the crude oil and natural gas that we produce.
Evolving expectations, regulations and related scrutiny regarding environmental, social and governance matters could impact our business and stock price.
paragraphs: We face risks in the normal course of business and through global, regional and local events that could have an adverse impact on our operations and financial performance. The following are some important risk factors that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected in any forward-looking statements. If any of the events or circumstances described in any of the following risk factors occurs, our business, results of operations and/or financial condition, as well as the trading price of our common stock and future prospects, could be materially and adversely affected, and our actual results may differ materially from those contemplated in any forward-looking statements we make in any public disclosures.

These risks reflect the Company's beliefs and opinions as to factors that could materially and adversely affect the Company and its securities in the future. References to past events are provided by way of example only and are not intended to be a complete listing or representation as to whether or not such factors have occurred in the past or their likelihood of occurring in the future. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties that we are unaware of, or that we currently believe are not material, may also become important factors that adversely affect our business.

Oil and natural gas prices are volatile and prolonged price declines could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, access to capital, and our ability to replace and grow future production.
Among the most significant variable factors impacting our business and financial condition are the sales prices for crude oil and natural gas that we produce.
Prices we receive for our oil and natural gas depend on numerous factors beyond our control, including, among others:
• domestic and global supply of and demand for oil and natural gas; • market uncertainty and consumer demand levels;

paragraphs: The following encompasses recent developments since the filing of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for year ended December 31, 2024:

Amended and Restated Credit Agreement — On January 20, 2026, we entered into the Amended and Restated Credit Agreement (the "A&R Credit Agreement") with a syndicate of financial institutions as lenders and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as administrative agent. The initial borrowing base and the total commitments are each $700 million. The A&R Credit Agreement replaces the Company's amended credit agreement dated May 10, 2018. See Part IV, Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules — Note 8 — Debt for additional information.

Lease Sale — The Big Beautiful Gulf 1 lease sale was held by BOEM on December 10, 2025. It was the first offshore oil and gas lease sale conducted under the new OBBBA. We emerged as the apparent high bidder on eleven of the twelve lease blocks on which we bid. As of February 17, 2026, we have been awarded eight of the lease blocks for which we were the high bidder and are awaiting BOEM's award decisions on our remaining high bids.

Surety Arrangements and Collateral Requirements — In early November 2025, we entered into various collateral funding and security arrangements ("CFSAs") to establish limits on the amount of aggregate collateral that our surety providers can require us to post. In exchange for our agreement to post the required amounts of collateral through July 1, 2031 and spend at least a specified amount on annual plugging and abandonment activities each year through 2030, the surety providers agreed not to (1) require additional collateral in excess of the agreed and scheduled amounts on existing surety bonds; (2) draw on collateral posted for the benefit of the sureties except under limited circumstances; (3) seek remedies for breaches of any surety agreement that are not an "Event of Default" as defined in the primary CFSA; or (4) cancel, or attempt to cancel, existing bonds unless requested by us.

For the three years commencing January 1, 2026 and for the subsequent two years commencing January 1, 2029, we are required to spend $90.0 million and $45.0 million on plugging and abandonment activities on an annual basis, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, our aggregate estimated collateral funding commitments under the CFSAs were $251.7 million through 2031. See Part IV, Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules — Note 15 — Commitments and Contingencies— Performance Obligations" for the estimated collateral funding commitments by year under the CFSAs. Also, see Item 7. "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations — Known Trends and Uncertainties — Financial Assurance Market Outlook."

The CFSAs generally contain certain events of default which, if triggered and not cured by us within the cure period, would terminate the standstill period and provide the sureties their full rights under their respective surety and indemnity agreements, including the right to call collateral. Events of default include, but are not limited to, the failure to maintain liquidity of $200.0 million or above a specified credit rating. However, if an event of default were to occur, it is anticipated we would be in a similar position than if we had not entered into the CFSAs given that the surety providers already have the right to demand collateral under existing surety bonds.

The CFSAs provide a multi-year framework to efficiently address the Company's collateral commitments and abandonment activities, while strengthening the relationship with our surety providers and supporting our long-term operational strategy.

Acquisition of Incremental Working Interest in Mississippi Canyon Blocks — On July 22, 2025, the Company completed the acquisition of an additional 75.2% and 50% working interest in U.S. Gulf of America Mississippi Canyon blocks 108 and 110, respectively, for $33.7 million of cash paid at closing. Prior to this acquisition, we owned an interest in and operated these developed and producing blocks. See Part IV, Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules — Note 3 — Acquisitions and Divestitures for additional information.

Enhanced Corporate Strategy — On June 17, 2025, we announced an enhanced corporate strategy designed to position the Company as a leading pure-play offshore exploration and production company. The strategy is built on three key pillars. The first pillar targets increased annualized free cash flow by improving our existing operations through capital efficiency, margin enhancement, commercial opportunities and general organizational improvements. The second pillar focuses on growth through high-margin organic projects and selective Deepwater acquisitions. The third pillar aims to build a long-lived and scaled portfolio in the U.S. Gulf of America and potentially other conventional basins. This strategy is underpinned by a disciplined capital allocation framework which prioritizes investing in projects expected to generate robust returns through commodity cycles, returning cash to shareholders, maintaining a strong balance sheet, and growing through selective opportunities.

Chief Financial Officer Transition — On May 16, 2025, Sergio L. Maiworm, Jr. informed the Board of Directors (the "Board") that he was resigning from his position as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of the Company, effective as of June 27, 2025. In connection with and following Mr. Maiworm's resignation, effective as of June 28, 2025, Gregory Babcock was appointed as Interim Chief Financial Officer to serve until a permanent Chief Financial Officer was appointed by the Board. On August 12, 2025,
the Board appointed Mr. Zachary B. Dailey to serve as the Company's Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer and principal financial officer, effective August 18, 2025.

Acquisition of Incremental Working Interest in Monument Oil Discovery — On March 7, 2025, the Company completed the acquisition of an incremental 8.3% working interest in the Monument oil discovery in the U.S. Gulf of America located on certain Walker Ridge lease blocks. See Part IV, Item 15. Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules — Note 3 — Acquisitions and Divestitures for additional information.

Appointment of President and Chief Executive Officer — Effective March 1, 2025, Mr. Paul Goodfellow was appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, principal executive officer and as an executive member of the Board.

Share Repurchase Program — During the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, we repurchased 12.6 million shares for $119.1 million exclusive of broker commissions under our share repurchase program, which was previously authorized by our Board, resulting in $80.9 million available under the share repurchase program. See "Liquidity and Capital Resources — Common Stock Repurchase Program" for additional information.

paragraphs: 以下為自我們於2024年12月31日財年結束後提交10-K年度報告後的近期發展情況：
修正並重述信貸協議 — 2026年1月20日，本公司與一羣金融機構作為貸款人及JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.作為行政代理簽訂了修正並重述信貸協議（"A&R信貸協議"）。初始借款基礎及總承諾金額各為700 百萬美元。A&R信貸協議取代了本公司於2018年5月10日簽訂的修正信貸協議。有關更多資訊，請參閱第四部分，第15項。附錄及財務報表附表 — 第8項 — 債務。
租賃出售 — 2025年12月10日，BOEM舉辦了Big Beautiful Gulf 1租賃出售。這是根據新OBBBA進行的首場離岸石油和天然氣租賃出售。我們在十二個租賃區塊中成為十一個區塊的顯著最高出價人。截至2026年2月17日，我們已獲頒八個我們為最高出價人的租賃區塊，並正在等待BOEM對我們剩餘最高出價的頒獎決定。

擔保安排與擔保要求 — 2025年11月初，本公司與各擔保機構簽訂了若干擔保資金與安全安排（"CFSAs"），以設定我們擔保機構可要求我們提交擔保總額的上限。作為我們同意在2031年7月1日前提交所需擔保金額，並每年至少投入指定金額用於年度封井與棄置活動至2030年，擔保機構同意不（1）要求超出協議及排程金額的額外擔保；（2）在有限情況除外下，動用為擔保機構提交的擔保；（3）尋求任何擔保協議的違約補救措施，除非該違約屬於主CFSA中定義的"違約事件"；或（4）取消或試圖取消現有擔保，除非我們要求。

自2026年1月1日起的三年，以及自2029年1月1日起的兩年，本公司每年必須投入90.0 百萬美元及45.0 百萬美元用於封井與棄置活動。截至2025年12月31日，本公司根據CFSAs的總預估擔保資金承諾為251.7 百萬美元至2031年。有關CFSAs下各年度預估擔保資金承諾，請參閱第四部分，第15項。附錄及財務報表附表 — 第15項 — 承諾與或有事項 — 服務義務。同時，請參閱第7項。"管理層對財務狀況與營運成果的討論與分析 — 已知趨勢與不確定性 — 財務保障市場展望。"
CFSAs一般包含某些違約事件，若觸發且本公司未能在寬限期內解決，將終止停滯期，並讓擔保機構行使其各自擔保與賠償協議下的全部權利，包括要求擔保的權利。違約事件包括但不限於未能維持200.0 百萬美元或以上的流動性或達成指定信用評級。然而，若發生違約事件，預期本公司將處於與未簽訂CFSAs時相似的狀態，因為擔保機構已擁有根據現有擔保協議要求擔保的權利。
CFSAs提供一個多年框架，以高效處理本公司的擔保承諾與棄置活動，同時加強與擔保機構的關係，並支持本公司長期營運策略。
取得密西西比峽灣區塊的增量工作權益 — 2025年7月22日，本公司完成了以現金33.7 百萬美元購入美國墨西哥灣美國墨西哥灣密西西比峽灣區塊108及110的額外75.2%及50%工作權益。在此次收購前，本公司已擁有這些開發中且正在生產的區塊的權益並進行經營。有關更多資訊，請參閱第四部分，第15項。附錄及財務報表附表 — 第3項 — 收購與出售。

強化企業戰略 — 2025 年 6 月 17 日，本公司宣佈了一項強化企業戰略，旨在將本公司定位為領先的純粹離岸探勘與生產公司。此戰略建立在三個關鍵支柱之上。第一個支柱目標為透過提高現有營運效率、邊際效益提升、商業機會及一般組織改善，增加年度自由現金流。第二個支柱著重於透過高邊際效益的內生性專案與選擇性深水區收購來實現成長。第三個支柱旨在於美國墨西哥灣及潛在其他傳統盆地建立長壽命且規模化的資產組合。此戰略以嚴謹的資本配置框架為基礎，優先投資預期能在商品週期中產生強勁回報的專案，回饋股東現金，維持強勁資產負債表，並透過選擇性機會實現成長。
財務長過渡 — 2025 年 5 月 16 日，Sergio L. Maiworm, Jr. 告知董事會（"董事會"）他將辭去本公司執行副總裁及財務長之職，生效日期為 2025 年 6 月 27 日。接續 Mr. Maiworm 辭職後，自 2025 年 6 月 28 日起，Gregory Babcock 被任命為臨時財務長，直至董事會任命永久財務長為止。2025 年 8 月 12 日，
董事會任命 Mr. Zachary B. Dailey 為本公司執行副總裁及財務長，並為主要財務官，生效日期為 2025 年 8 月 18 日。
取得 Monument 油田發現的增量作業權益 — 2025 年 3 月 7 日，本公司完成取得位於美國墨西哥灣 Walker Ridge 租賃區塊的 Monument 油田發現的增量 8.3% 作業權益。有關更多資訊，請參閱第四部分，第 15 項。附錄與財務明細表 — 備註 3 — 收購與出售。
董事長及首席執行官任命 — 自 2025 年 3 月 1 日起，Mr. Paul Goodfellow 被任命為董事長及首席執行官，並為主要執行官，同時成為董事會執行成員。
股票買回計畫 — 在 2025 年 12 月 31 日結訖的十二個月內，本公司於股票買回計畫下，扣除經紀佣金後，買回 12.6 百萬股，總金額為 119.1 百萬美元，因此股票買回計畫下尚有 80.9 百萬美元可用。有關更多資訊，請參閱 "流動性及資本資源 — 普通股買回計畫"。

headings: 與本公司業務及石油與天然氣產業相關之風險
若我們無法替換石油與天然氣儲備，我們可能無法維持或成長本公司業務。
未來探勘與鑽井結果具有不確定性，且涉及重大成本。
本公司目前營運主要集中於單一地理區域，使我們面臨區域性風險。
全球地緣政治緊張關係可能增加石油、天然氣與NGL價格之波動性，並可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。
本公司實際回收之儲備可能與本公司已證儲備估計值有顯著差異。
若我們無法在租約到期前進行鑽井，我們可能喪失租約。
我們依賴基礎建設以行銷與交付本公司之生產量。
通貨膨脹及利率變動可能增加我們的成本。
我們可能無法以合理可接受的條件取得足夠的擔保債券以進行業務運作。
科技與網路安全威脅可能幹擾我們的營運，並對我們的業務造成聲譽及財務損失。
我們對不直接經營的不動產之活動控制有限。
避險交易可能限制我們的潛在獲利，並使我們面臨其他風險。
遵守環境法規，包括與海洋生物及受威脅及瀕危物種相關的法律要求，可能增加我們的成本並限制營運。
生產停工可能增加成本並降低未來產量。
極端天氣或公共衛生事件可能幹擾生產並減少收入。
本公司未對所有可能影響營運之風險投保。
實際生產量可能與預測有重大差異。
產業激烈競爭可能限制本公司成長並提高成本。
失去重要客戶可能導致營業收入大幅減少，並對本公司業務造成重大不利影響。
本公司依賴具專業技能與經驗之人力，若發生人力短缺、勞動成本上升或關鍵管理階層流失，可能影響本公司營運能力。
本公司有各種契約義務，若無法履行這些義務，可能對營運成果與財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
本公司在墨西哥之營運業務受制於不斷演進之法規與環境要求，可能增加成本並產生合規風險。
地震資料解譯無法保證存在具商業價值之液態烴氣藏。
違反反貪污法規，包括美國外國腐敗行為規避法，可能會導致嚴重處罰及喪失重要契約。
我們的業務面臨與氣候變遷相關風險，可能會提高我們的營運成本、限制我們可經營的地區，並降低我們生產的原油及天然氣需求。
有關環境、社會及治理事項的演進期望、法規及相關監管 scrutiny，可能會影響我們的業務及股票價格。
paragraphs: 我們在正常業務運作中以及透過全球、區域及地方事件面臨風險，這些事件可能對我們的營運及財務表現產生不利影響。以下為一些重要的風險因素，這些因素可能導致我們的實際結果與任何前瞻性陳述中預期的結果有重大差異。如果發生任何在下列風險因素中所描述的事件或情況，將可能對我們的業務、營運結果及財務狀況，以及我們普通股的交易價格與未來展望產生重大且不利的影響，而我們的實際結果可能與任何前瞻性陳述中所預期的結果有重大差異。
這些風險反映本公司對可能對本公司及其證券在未來產生重大且不利影響的因素的信念與觀點。提及過去事件僅作為範例，並非意圖提供完整的清單或表示這些因素是否曾在過去發生或其未來發生的可能性。下列所描述的風險與不確定性並非我們所面臨的唯一風險。我們可能還會面臨其他風險與不確定性，這些風險與不確定性可能是我們目前未察覺，或我們目前認為不具重大性，但未來可能成為影響我們業務的重要因素。
原油與天然氣價格波動性很高，若價格持續下跌，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果、現金流、取得資金的能力，以及我們替換與增長未來產能的能力產生重大且不利的影響。
